focus: Which diagram design rules in sk-design-diagram and sk-design-fundamentals have no counterpart in the FigJam packet, and which of those gaps can a FigJam board actually carry?
answeredQuestions: Which diagram design rules in sk-design-diagram and sk-design-fundamentals have no counterpart in the FigJam packet, and which of those gaps can a FigJam board actually carry?

label: The comparator fixes a minimum gap between nodes as a number (24 standard, 40 presentation, 24 print) plus a 40px outer margin; the FigJam packet states no gap, and because the generator owns geometry the carryable form is a model-side constraint that protects the gap (fewer nodes per rank, shorter labels), not a gap measurement.

Proximity is the comparator's named fix for ambiguous grouping - more space around a group than within it - and the FigJam packet has no proximity rule at all: a status tint is drawn 24px larger on every side but the packet never states its relationship to the contents' own spacing, so a tint can hug nodes 200px apart and read as a loose rectangle.

The comparator mandates zoning above 9 nodes (2-4 labeled zones, hairline border, uppercase zone label at top-left) because an unzoned 20-node diagram is a wiring diagram; the FigJam packet only ever splits, so no type has a middle option between one diagram and two, and a board of split diagrams has no visible relationship between its parts.

The comparator has five mandatory connector rules (orthogonal elbows, 6-10px label gap with opaque mask, no shared stroke path, fanned attach points 12px apart, never route behind a non-endpoint box); the FigJam packet has one crossing counter, and although the generator routes, the model can still create the failure conditions - long connector labels in a dense rank, two edges between one pair, a declaration order that forces a long reach - and names none of them.

The comparator carries a density dial with a stated target (4/10, 'enough to be technically complete, not so dense it needs a guide'); the FigJam packet has ceilings only (9 nodes, 12 gantt tasks, 5 parallel bars), so a board drawn at 2/10 and a board drawn at 9/10 pass the same check.

Shape-as-hierarchy is a hard comparator rule that four of seven FigJam types cannot satisfy - sequence has lifelines, ER one table shape, state rounded states, gantt bars - so in those types every same-kind node draws identically and all hierarchy must arrive from the optional extension layer, which the packet never states.

The comparator requires a legend that covers every type used and nothing extra; the FigJam legend is a column of numbered stickies covering annotations only, and the bottom strip is listed as a deliberate omission, so a board using four shapes, a lane and a tint has a legend for none of them and the reader must infer the vocabulary.

The comparator requires a per-diagram title of about 60 characters and a one-sentence description of what the diagram shows in reader terms; the FigJam packet has all three equivalents already in play - the generator name, the userIntent sentence sent on every call, and the optional title text node - but no contract tying them together or putting the intent sentence on the board or in the reply.

The comparator's review contract demands a location, the offending value and a fix per finding, and a count of zero per tier rather than an omitted tier; the FigJam scorecard produces seven numbers with one reason each, so Layout 1 cannot be repaired from the score and an unexamined dimension scores a silent 2.

The comparator scales its type ramp with reading distance and draws the consequence that a presentation ramp implies fewer nodes; the FigJam packet claims two dials because the board fixes format and size, which is right about format and optimistic about size, since a board read on a wall or holding six diagrams is further away while its node names cannot grow.

The comparator's status treatment is dark text on a light tint because it sits quietly in the hierarchy, and the FigJam accent pairs already measure 11:1 to 14:1 for text on fill, which is a strength; but the status tint recipe paints a group at accent saturation, multiplying over a group the area the style guide already admits sits under the 3:1 mark gate.

The comparator's strongest instruction - never reproduce a renderer's layout, replace automatic spacing and routing - is one the FigJam packet must refuse, because the generator is the only route for architecture; the transferable part is narrower: the comparator rejects automatic spacing that ignores grouping, and a board can honour that by giving the generator a model with fewer competing ranks and a visible grouping.

direction: Adopt 'replace the renderer layout' as a FigJam rule
reason: generate_diagram is the only route for architecture and the packet's type files depend on it; the transferable intent is constraining the model so the generator's default layout is good.

direction: Re-add the horizontal legend strip and viewBox expansion
reason: A board has no viewBox; the board-native form is a legend group visible without scrolling.

direction: Re-add the four-dial output spec verbatim
reason: Format and size do not transfer as written; only the reading-distance consequence of the size dial does.
